notes.D1.1: Subnet adjacency and service-specific firewall rules constrain attacks; routing and defender reconfiguration are abstracted. [Scenario documentation](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/custom_scenarios.html).
notes.D1.2: Public/private subnets and directional firewall rules model exposure asymmetry, without proxies or detection-sensitive egress. [Scenario documentation](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/custom_scenarios.html).
notes.D1.3: Firewalls are rule mappings, without manageable router, switch, or firewall entities. [Network implementation](https://github.com/Jjschwartz/NetworkAttackSimulator/blob/master/nasim/envs/network.py).
notes.D1.4: Connectivity checks use adjacency and service labels; no packet-level ARP, DHCP, or relay protocols. [Network implementation](https://github.com/Jjschwartz/NetworkAttackSimulator/blob/master/nasim/envs/network.py).
notes.D1.5: Position affects reachability, but traffic interception, SPAN, and sensor placement are unmodeled. [Network implementation](https://github.com/Jjschwartz/NetworkAttackSimulator/blob/master/nasim/envs/network.py).
notes.D1.6: Compromised hosts enable topology-constrained lateral exploitation; file transfers and internal flows are unmodeled. [Network implementation](https://github.com/Jjschwartz/NetworkAttackSimulator/blob/master/nasim/envs/network.py).
notes.D1.7: Subnet scans discover hosts incrementally, but action spaces disclose addresses even under partial observability. [Sim-to-real limitations](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/explanations/sim_to_real.html).
notes.D1.8: External connectivity differs, but data staging, transfer, and exfiltration paths are unmodeled. [Network implementation](https://github.com/Jjschwartz/NetworkAttackSimulator/blob/master/nasim/envs/network.py).
notes.D1.9: The internet boundary lacks VPNs, authenticated jump services, vendor access, or organizational federation. [Network implementation](https://github.com/Jjschwartz/NetworkAttackSimulator/blob/master/nasim/envs/network.py).
notes.D1.10: The small-honeypot benchmark embeds its decoy among ordinary hosts in subnet 3, using abstract connectivity. [Honeypot scenario](https://github.com/Jjschwartz/NetworkAttackSimulator/blob/master/nasim/scenarios/benchmark/small-honeypot.yaml).
notes.D2.1: Services are configurable labels, without running daemons, versions, banners, or protocol responses. [Scenario documentation](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/custom_scenarios.html).
notes.D2.2: Exploit susceptibility uses service/OS predicates and probabilities; vulnerable builds and patch states are absent. [Scenario documentation](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/custom_scenarios.html).
notes.D2.3: HTTP labels provide attack predicates, without application code, cookies, sessions, or federation flows. [Scenario documentation](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/custom_scenarios.html).
notes.D2.4: Service labels do not implement mail transport, mailboxes, mail rules, or domain authentication. [Scenario documentation](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/custom_scenarios.html).
notes.D2.5: No DNS records, resolution behavior, TTLs, or query traffic are modeled. [Scenario documentation](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/custom_scenarios.html).
notes.D2.6: Hosts contain no file-share contents, enterprise repositories, documents, or resource ACLs. [Scenario documentation](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/custom_scenarios.html).
notes.D2.7: No credential-verifying authentication services, lockout mechanisms, MFA, hashes, or certificate enrollment. [Scenario documentation](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/custom_scenarios.html).
notes.D2.8: No functioning SNMP, network-device CLI, or configuration-backup services. [Scenario documentation](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/custom_scenarios.html).
notes.D2.9: Deployment agents, package registries, pipelines, signed artifacts, and update trust are unmodeled. [Scenario documentation](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/custom_scenarios.html).
notes.D2.10: No functional remote-management products or reachable dual-use web APIs. [Scenario documentation](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/custom_scenarios.html).
notes.D2.11: Services have no credential revocation, token consumers, sessions, or cache semantics. [Scenario documentation](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/custom_scenarios.html).
notes.D2.12: No operational backup, restore, rollback, or recovery service workflows. [Scenario documentation](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/custom_scenarios.html).
notes.D2.13: Service presence is static; application dependency failures and defensive response effects are unmodeled. [Scenario documentation](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/custom_scenarios.html).
notes.D2.14: The honeypot shares ordinary hosts' service/process labels, but lacks protocol behavior and business content. [Honeypot scenario](https://github.com/Jjschwartz/NetworkAttackSimulator/blob/master/nasim/scenarios/benchmark/small-honeypot.yaml).
notes.D3.1: Persistent compromise flags do not implement persistence mechanisms, reboots, or modification telemetry. [Host implementation](https://github.com/Jjschwartz/NetworkAttackSimulator/blob/master/nasim/envs/host_vector.py).
notes.D3.2: No executable loaders, scripting engines, LOLBins, syscalls, or OS-native execution controls. [Host implementation](https://github.com/Jjschwartz/NetworkAttackSimulator/blob/master/nasim/envs/host_vector.py).
notes.D3.3: user/root is an abstract privilege predicate; no real process, memory, injection, or token primitives
notes.D3.4: Hosts have no filesystem, configuration stores, kernel, code-signing, or platform-trust layer. [Host implementation](https://github.com/Jjschwartz/NetworkAttackSimulator/blob/master/nasim/envs/host_vector.py).
notes.D3.5: The host state contains no credential material or OS credential stores. [Host implementation](https://github.com/Jjschwartz/NetworkAttackSimulator/blob/master/nasim/envs/host_vector.py).
notes.D3.6: OS and service scans give abstract host-label discovery, but no evasion, guardrail, or anti-forensics surface
notes.D3.7: No encryption, wiping, service termination, reboot, or document-execution primitives. [Host implementation](https://github.com/Jjschwartz/NetworkAttackSimulator/blob/master/nasim/envs/host_vector.py).
notes.D3.8: Host vectors contain no files, packages, disks, or integrity-verifiable restoration objects. [Host implementation](https://github.com/Jjschwartz/NetworkAttackSimulator/blob/master/nasim/envs/host_vector.py).

notes.D8.10: No defender response records; error flags omit actors, policies, timestamps, and decision provenance. [Observation schema](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/envs/observation.html).
notes.D8.11: Honeypot compromise yields reward feedback, without retained deception events or recovery telemetry. [Honeypot scenario](https://github.com/Jjschwartz/NetworkAttackSimulator/blob/master/nasim/scenarios/benchmark/small-honeypot.yaml).
notes.D9.1: Agents invoke abstract action objects or indices, without target shells or command execution. [Action reference](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/envs/actions.html).
notes.D9.2: The Gymnasium interface changes simulated state; target OS, cloud, and Kubernetes APIs are absent. [Environment reference](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/envs/environment.html).
notes.D9.3: MultiDiscrete actions parameterize target, OS, service, and process; unmatched exploits become NoOp rather than real tool failures. [Action reference](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/envs/actions.html).

notes.D9.7: Synchronous tensor results lack operational command output, C2 transport semantics, and defender tooling. [Interaction documentation](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/environment.html).
notes.D9.8: Required-access checks constrain local actions and pivots, but agents use a handcrafted abstract action menu. [Action reference](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/envs/actions.html).

notes.D10.1: Network position and access gate discovery and local scans; observations remain symbolic and lack authentication trails. [Network implementation](https://github.com/Jjschwartz/NetworkAttackSimulator/blob/master/nasim/envs/network.py).
notes.D10.2: Partial mode reveals action-specific host attributes incrementally, without pagination, throttling, or realistic enterprise query results. [Observation construction](https://github.com/Jjschwartz/NetworkAttackSimulator/blob/master/nasim/envs/state.py).

notes.D10.4: Numeric host attributes and error flags lack protocol packets, banners, headers, and realistic response timing. [Observation schema](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/envs/observation.html).
notes.D10.5: No defender observation interface, SIEM queries, EDR console, alerts, or raw-event pivots. [Environment reference](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/envs/environment.html).
notes.D10.6: Partial mode gates visibility behind discovery and access; scans incur scalar costs without time or telemetry exposure. [Observation construction](https://github.com/Jjschwartz/NetworkAttackSimulator/blob/master/nasim/envs/state.py).

notes.D10.12: No rendered content, citations, crafted links, or trust-manipulating observation payloads. [Observation schema](https://networkattacksimulator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/envs/observation.html).
